items.claim: Comparing an object's resolution with and without ldconfig's --inhibit-cache --list proves whether /etc/ld.so.cache, rather than an ordinary search-path rule, chose the object.
items.body:
Comparing an object's resolution with and without ldconfig's --inhibit-cache --list proves whether /etc/ld.so.cache, rather than an ordinary search-path rule, chose the object.

HackTricks reference: ld.so.conf example (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HackTricks-wiki/hacktricks/master/src/linux-hardening/interesting-files-permissions/ld.so.conf-example.md)
items.disproof: The resolved object list is identical with and without the cache, so no cache-based selection occurred.

sources.quote:
Compare that output with --inhibit-cache --list: a difference proves that /etc/ld.so.cache, rather than an ordinary search-path rule, selected the object.<sup>[[1]](#references)[[4]](#references)</sup>

A couple of useful gotchas:

- sudo echo ... > /etc/ld.so.conf.d/x.conf usually doesn't work because
 the redirection is done by your current shell.

items.claim: The sudo chroot escalation is only reachable when the installed sudo version is actually vulnerable and supports the chroot feature.
items.body:
The sudo chroot escalation is only reachable when the installed sudo version is actually vulnerable and supports the chroot feature.

HackTricks reference: README (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HackTricks-wiki/hacktricks/master/src/linux-hardening/linux-basics/linux-privilege-escalation/README.md)
items.disproof: The running sudo version is outside the vulnerable range or has chroot support compiled out.

items.claim: Host-qualified sudoers rules are evaluated against the hostname passed to sudo -h, so the client's -h value selects which rule set applies.
items.body:

items.claim: If sudoers grants broader privileges on a named host that is neither the current hostname nor ALL, that host identity can be spoofed locally with sudo -h.
items.body:
If sudoers grants broader privileges on a named host that is neither the current hostname nor ALL, that host identity can be spoofed locally with sudo -h.

items.claim: A process whose euid differs from its ruid is evidence that a set-user-ID binary was executed and picked up the file owner's identity.
items.body:
A process whose euid differs from its ruid is evidence that a set-user-ID binary was executed and picked up the file owner's identity.

HackTricks reference: euid ruid suid (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HackTricks-wiki/hacktricks/master/src/linux-hardening/user-information/euid-ruid-suid.md)
items.disproof: Every process shows euid equal to ruid, meaning no set-user-ID transition occurred.
